pr.title: perf: serialize pull/push on a shared background executor; guard invokeAndWait exceptions

report.summary: This PR moves pull/push entry points off the EDT and centralizes error/info dialog creation into uiRun/showError/showInfo helpers in Plugin.kt, and hardens dialogConflictResolver's invokeAndWait usage with InterruptedException/InvocationTargetException handling in ConflictResolvers.kt; test call sites are updated to the new internal pull()/push() methods. Reviewers should focus on whether the new threading actually serializes concurrent pull/push invocations (the PR description claims a shared single-thread executor, but the diff uses kotlin.concurrent.thread per click) and on which work now runs on the event dispatch thread.

suggestions.title: Menu/key actions spawn a new thread per click instead of submitting to a serializing executor
suggestions.reason: The diff replaces `uiRun(this::pull)` with `this.context?.guiContext?.addMenuAction("Pull") { kotlin.concurrent.thread { this.pull() } }` (and the same pattern at lines 45, 50 and 54 for Push and both key bindings). This contradicts the stated design of a shared single-thread `backgroundExecutor`: every menu click or key press creates a brand-new thread, so rapid activations still run `pull()`/`push()` concurrently and can interleave repository reads/writes and project mutations — exactly the corruption case this PR claims to fix. Additionally `kotlin.concurrent.thread` defaults to `isDaemon = false`, so the hung/blocked worker also prevents JVM shutdown, contrary to the description's daemon-thread rationale.
suggestions.failure_scenario: A user double-clicks the Pull menu item (or presses ctrl+BACK_SLASH twice quickly). Two independent threads enter pull(), both call readLocalRepository()/projectToLocalRepository()/writeLocalRepository() on the same on-disk repository, and interleaved writes leave the local repository in a partially updated or inconsistent state.
